A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Visual Iconicity Challenge. Their main text, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison. Appendices A–F correspond directly; v3 adds Appendix G.

before.justification: v1 reports original VLM evaluations and collected human phonology and transparency baselines in Sections 3–6 and Appendices E–F.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds evaluations of further models, a thinking-mode comparison, cross-task correlations and qualitative error analysis.

M1.justification: The proposed benchmark retains its three tasks, phonological label scheme and task prompts, including unchanged Appendices B–C. The thinking-mode experiment evaluates an additional configuration of an off-the-shelf model rather than introducing a new proposed model or benchmark method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 96 isolated NGT signs on phonology, transparency and iconicity, including both transparency choice conditions. Appendix A's stimuli and ratings are identical. Corrected subtype counts and newly disclosed Turkish participant backgrounds do not establish additional data or population coverage.

E2.justification: The main panel changes from 13 to 17 models: Qwen3-VL-32B/4B, MiMo-VL-7B, GPT-5.4, Gemini 3 Flash and Gemini 3.1 Pro are added, while LLaVA-Video-7B/72B disappear from Tables 3, 4 and 8. Comparator subsets also change in Figures 4 and 8. Few-shot Table 5 adds Qwen3-VL-32B and MiMo but removes Qwen2.5-VL-7B.

E3.justification: v3 replaces Cohen's d with quadratic-weighted kappa for zero-shot iconicity and removes d from few-shot Table 5, while retaining Spearman correlation. It adds a thinking-on/off condition and changes Figure 7's inclusion threshold from more than three to at least seven models. The underlying 96-sign and four-exemplar designs remain.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained few-shot and iconicity-type analyses, v3 adds a thinking-mode ablation, quantified phonology–iconicity and phonology–transparency associations in Section 6, and qualitative error analysis in Appendix G. Table 9 introduces Missing Agent, Static Bias and Gloss Sensitivity cases, substantially expanding the diagnostic analyses.

E5.justification: v3 adds standard-error bars to Figure 4 and identifies Figure 3's uncertainty as binomial SEs over 96 signs. v1 already displayed Figure 3 error bars without defining them. Correlation significance reporting is retained; neither version documents repeated-run counts or seeds.

E6.justification: New model results change the panel's best transparency accuracy from 0.177 to 0.292 and best iconicity correlation from 0.607 to 0.774; these are different-model results, not same-model improvements. v3 adds kappa and thinking-mode outcomes while removing Qwen2.5-VL-7B's 0.456-to-0.321 few-shot decline. Most shared scores remain unchanged. Its new claim that Qwen3-VL-32B leads open-model 96-option transparency contradicts Table 3, where Qwen2.5-VL-32B scores 0.052 versus 0.042.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theoretical results or proofs. The added standard agreement metric and empirical correlations do not introduce mathematical definitions, derivations or formal properties.

C1.justification: The central benchmark contribution and diagnostic claims remain. v3 adds an abstract/conclusion claim that explicit reasoning narrows the open-to-closed-model calibration gap, and broadens the reported iconicity alignment from moderate to moderate-to-strong. These extend the conclusions without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v3 develops a substantial distinction between rank alignment and scale agreement, interprets thinking mode as repairing scale anchoring, and extends the phonology discussion to meaning inference. Appendix G adds agent-mapping and culturally specific gloss explanations. It also clarifies the Turkish deaf signer's baseline as cross-linguistic inference. The original limitations subsection is largely retained.

D1.justification: Section 4 newly documents video frame rate and duration, eight-frame sampling across models, and a Qwen3 token/context-budget example. Participant background, course-credit compensation, consent and ethics approval are also disclosed. These improve documentation without establishing that retained experiments were rerun; prompts, hardware information and repository access largely persist.

R1.justification: The related-work survey and first-systematic-benchmark positioning largely persist. v3 adds Ortega and Özyürek (2020), Zhou et al. (2025) and references for added models, while removing references including Liu et al. (2024) and Lugaresi et al. (2019). It more explicitly positions the contribution as exposing a linguistic consequence of known static visual bias.

P1.justification: The overall section sequence and much of the dataset and related-work prose remain. The abstract, results and conclusion are revised; Section 6 is retitled and subdivided, and an Ethics Statement and Appendix G are added. Terminology and correspondence details receive smaller edits. This is a targeted revision rather than wholesale narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: Figures 3–5 and 7–8 are substantially redrawn for revised model panels, with changed styling, labels and captions; Figure 4 gains error bars and Figure 8 reorders its axes. Tables 4–5 change metric columns, Table 8 introduces model groups, and Table 9 is new. Table 1 and Figure 2 move while retaining their content.

improvement.justification: v3 makes calibration claims easier to evaluate through ordinal-agreement scores and a reasoning-mode comparison, and documents video inputs more clearly. These support a limited improvement. Reporting regressions temper the gains: Figures 3 and 8 mislabel the unchanged hearing-nonexpert baseline as deaf-native, Figure 7 shows 19 models identifying TELEPHONE despite the stated 17-model panel, and Table 5 omits the earlier negative Qwen2.5-VL-7B few-shot result.
